
=================================================================
#74 Buyeo Euija†  (660 December)
Arc: Part III — Kingfall / The Fall of Baekje · place: changan · tone: psychopomp ritual
Logline: In the Tang capital, a confession is already written. There’s a space at the bottom for his name.
=================================================================
[0] ¶ An empire is not finished with a king until he has signed something.
[1] ¶ In Chang’an, on the first morning of winter, Euija is brought forth before the Third Emperor.
[2] ¶ First, paperwork. A palace clerk hands the prisoner a confession, already written out in a fair hand. There is a space at the bottom for his name.
[3] Tang clerk: Aloud, please. Clearly. The scribes are taking it down.
[4] King Euija: ‘I, the criminal Euija, having been liberated by the Great Tang—’ / Liberated. Hm. So that’s what that was. / ‘—confess with gratitude that without the Great Tang there would be no New Baekje—’ / There isn’t one. You burned it. / ‘—and resolve to serve the Emperor for ten thousand years.’ / Ten thousand? I’m sixty. Ambitious fellow, your clerk.
[5] King Euija: It’s a bad story. Nobody’s afraid of anything, there’s no villain, and the hero is a building. / Who wrote this? I’ve done better drunk.
[6] Tang clerk: Your name, please. Here.
[7] ¶ He signs in a hand so large the name runs off the edge of the paper, and gives it back. The clerk files it without looking. A confession only needs a name, and has never much minded whose.
[8] ❝QUOTE (Zizhi Tongjian (資治通鑑) bk. 200, Tang Gaozong, Xianqing 5 (660), eleventh month): Eleventh month, first day. The emperor went up to the Zetian Gate tower to receive the Baekje captives, and released them all, from their king Euija down.❞
[9] King Euija: Kim Chunchu… / **KIM CHUNCHU!!!**
[10] ¶ Across the sea, in Surabol, King Muyeol is eating his supper.
[11] King Muyeol: Hm?
[12] King Euija: **Kim Chunchu, you wretch!!** / **You vile traitor of the ages, who dragged a foreign power onto the soil of Samhan!!** / **Heaven’s punishment will find you!!**
[13] ¶ The shouting burns out. What remains is a man who has finally run out of stories to sell — and one last story he cannot afford to keep.
[14] King Euija: Let someone… avenge me…! / Let someone… raise Baekje again…! / Chunchu — what you finished… may it never stay finished…!
[15] ¶ He is shouting at the man who won. Across the sea, a quiet son with lovely handwriting is still waiting to be needed.
[16] ¶ Then the room fills with men only he can see.
[17] King Euija: Gods are props. Spirits are lighting. / Heh… so you guys are real after all…
[18] Haewonmek: Any last words?
[19] ¶ Euija waits. He has always been good at making a room lean in.
[20] King Euija: No.
[21] ¶ Kangrim reads his name three times in the Tang capital — Euija. Euija. Euija. — the underworld's receipt before the humiliation finishes.
[22] Kangrim: Eraha. King. / One question, then we walk. / They called you the Zengzi of the East. You hung a dragon over the Sabi for a crowd. Which were you?
[23] King Euija: …The dragon. Obviously. / Several hundred people saw the dragon. Nobody ever saw a Zengzi do anything.
[24] Kangrim: The boy at the White River. / The name you gave him is still in the ledger.
[25] King Euija: …A friend. / Put the miracle on the cheap side of the page.
[26] ▼ FLASHBACK 632 The river · 백강
    [26.0] ¶ A jar in a hedge, and a prince who ought to be at his own investiture.
    [26.1] ¶ A grey hood at the back of a crowd. A boy going into black water on a rope.
    [26.2] King Euija: How many times have you gone in?
    [26.3] Gyebek: Nineteen.
    [26.4] ¶ A pale deer in the reeds, standing where nobody else is up to see it.
    [26.5] Gyebek: …Do you like the name, or do you like me?
[26] ▲ end flashback
[27] King Euija: …You. / It was you, you idiot. The name was just the best thing I had on me.
[28] Kangrim: He is waiting at the ford. Tell him yourself. He will want it said exactly. / Then you die richer than the record will admit. / Come.
[29] ¶ Euija dies, vengeful and emptied. Then, at the very last, neither.
[30] ¶ _Thus was the end of Buyeo Euija._
[31] ¶ _A man the court once called the Zengzi of the East._
[32] ❝QUOTE (Jiu Tangshu (舊唐書) bk. 199A, Eastern Barbarians — Baekje): Euija served his parents with a devotion people talked about, and was kind to his brothers; men of his time called him the Zeng and Min of the East. He reached the capital and died a few days later.❞
[33] ¶ — Buyeo Euija —
[34] ¶ _Seongchung told him. He put Seongchung in a cell. Heungsu told him. He had already exiled Heungsu. Gyebek would have told him, and he had put Gyebek on a boat. A man does not fall because nobody warned him. He falls because he arranged, patiently and over years, to be somewhere the warnings could not reach._
[35] ¶ _The Zengzi of the East. They called him that when he was young, and they meant it. The name was neither flattery nor wrong. He was never a fool. He was a clever man who won, and kept winning, until winning was the only instrument he had left, and then he tried to play a dying country on it._
[36] ¶ **Baekje is gone. Goguryeo still stands. And the man who arranged both can no longer get out of bed…?**
